Summary

“She was born premature,” Mydei said quietly, “Hyacine said there may be some difficulties in her development.”

Phainon stared at Eleni's face, and already knew he would do anything for her.

“Don't worry,” he promised Mydei, “We'll take care of her. We'll give her the best life we can.”

Or, Phainon and Mydei are blessed with a daughter. She exists in some cycles. She doesn't in others.

Khaslana witnesses it all.

chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.html:
Her first existence began in the 56th cycle.

She was born into their crumbling world with a cry that split the air, but had quickly calmed down as soon as she was placed into Mydei's arms. It was as if being nestled against her mother's bosom was all she needed, seeming to find all the warmth and safety the world could offer in that single embrace.

“Eleni,” Mydei had said, when Hyacine asked for the baby's name, “Our shining light.”

“She's beautiful,” were the first words that left Phainon's mouth when he laid his eyes on her. His blue eyes were wide and shimmering with a mixture of awe and disbelief, as if he couldn't quite believe what he was seeing. Hyacine had already slipped out of the room with a knowing smile, giving them some privacy.

“She looks just like you, Mydei.”

Despite being exhausted, Mydei mustered a proud grin.

“Seems like my genes won out,” he commented, before glancing down at their daughter and adjusting her swaddle. “Deliverer. Come hold her.”

Phainon blinked rapidly, suddenly overcome by a wave of nerves, “Me? Now? I—”

Mydei clicked his tongue, interrupting him smoothly. “Sit down,” he instructed, “Arms like this. Be careful.”

Phainon gnawed his lower lip hesitantly, but did as told. When Mydei gently deposited Eleni in his waiting arms, he immediately felt a surge of emotion well up in his chest. It felt like he was holding the entire world in his hands.

“She's so small,” Phainon murmured after a beat of studying his sleeping daughter's face. She was impossibly tiny snuggled up in his arms. Her entire body was probably only the size of his elbow. “I don't think babies are supposed to be this small.”

“She was born premature,” Mydei said quietly, “Hyacine said there may be some difficulties in her development.”

Phainon stared at Eleni's face, and already knew he would do anything for her.

“Don't worry,” he promised Mydei, “We'll take care of her. We'll give her the best life we can.”

The smile Mydei gave him was engraved into Phainon's memory.

Eleni was two years old when Khaslana first met her.

The appearance of an anomaly never seen before in any of the previous fifty-something cycles was enough to stun Khaslana for a moment.

He knew Phainon and Mydei loved each other, but the progress of their relationship varied across all cycles. In some, they became lovers and shared a bed. In others, they tiptoed the edge, neither daring to profess their feelings due to the prophecy looming over their heads. Some cycles they never became aware of each other's feelings at all, and the distance between them remained until Khaslana arrived to stop Era Nova.

Khaslana didn't recognise her at first. The child didn't even reach his knees, and he probably wouldn't have even noticed her if he didn't pay keen attention to his surroundings. Although she was small, her blonde hair was meticulously tied into pigtails, and her fine clothes proved that her caretakers had dressed her with much love and care.

Clothes that were bound to end up covered in dirt if she didn't walk properly. She was still unsteady on her feet, toddling around with all the energy in the world but with none of the coordination.

When she looked like she was close to tripping, Khaslana rushed forward without thinking. “Careful,” he murmured, gingerly steadying the child back on her feet.

Eleni blinked up at him. She had the golden, flaming eyes of a man Khaslana was all too familiar with.

The first thought that came to Khaslana’s mind was that her birth must've been an accident. Although Phainon and Mydei had crossed the barriers of simple comradery and became lovers in some cycles, under no circumstances would they have willingly brought a child into this world at this point of time. The Flame-Chase Journey was ongoing and the threats of the black tide still raged.

As Chrysos Heirs who had yet to inherit their respective coreflames and undergo the divine trials, there was far too much to do, far too many burdens to carry. This was not an adequate time and setting to have a child.

Khaslana stared at her. From the child’s appearance alone, it was clear she was well cared for. Her parents might have carried the weight of the world on their shoulders, yet it seemed they had never neglected their duty to her.

“Papa,” Eleni said suddenly, extending her small arms towards him. Khaslana froze at the word, his breath catching in his throat, but the little girl only looked up at him with unguarded trust and shining hope in her beautiful eyes, an innocence still untainted by this cruel world.

Right. Khaslana looked like Phainon. Eleni must’ve thought Khaslana was her father.

Before Khaslana could say something, tell her that no, he was not her father even though he looked identical to him, he heard the sound of pounding footsteps approaching, cutting through the storm of turmoil brewing in his head.

“Eleni!” A frantic voice that sounded just like his own yelled at the top of their lungs. Khaslana stiffened. He needed to go.

Phainon burst into view a moment later, breathless and sweat-damp, his snow white hair tousled. When he saw Eleni, his shoulders sagged in palpable relief.

“You scared the life out of me!” he exclaimed, hurrying towards her. Dropping to a crouch, he cupped her face with trembling hands, his eyes darting over her to make sure she was unhurt. “I take my eyes off you for one second and you’re gone. How do you even run so fast with such little legs?”

“Papa?” Eleni asked, sounding confused. She looked behind her, but Khaslana was gone.

“Yeah? I'm right here, princess,” Phainon pressed a kiss to her hair, sighing and holding her tight. “Let's go home. Mydei's waiting.”

Eleni's eyes lit up, “Mama?”

“Mhm. Mama’s waiting. I'm sure he misses us.”

Hidden in the shadows, Khaslana watched where they stood a few moments ago.

In this cycle, he had a daughter. A family he shared with the man he loved.

His heart twisted in his chest. Khaslana turned away, departing without a glance back. This was not his scene to linger in. Not his happiness to claim.

After all, the Phainon of this cycle, of every cycle, was on borrowed time. Khaslana should let them have their happiness, fleeting as it was. Let them and the rest of the Chrysos Heirs bask in this illusion of peace while it lasted.

Cycle 108th. Era Nova was prevented once more.

There was a bone-deep weariness in Khaslana's shoulders, but there was nothing he could do except persevere. The coreflames hummed inside him, and that was all the reminder he needed to keep moving forward.

In this cycle, Eleni was born once more.

Khaslana had not forgotten her face. The faces of all the Chrysos Heirs were etched in his mind forevermore, but even though he'd met Eleni briefly only once, his fleeting memory of her features had never faded. She looked like Mydei, after all. And if there was anyone Khaslana would never forget, it would be Mydei.

When he first saw her again, she was only a baby. Probably not even a year old.

Having succumbed to his hideous selfishness, Khaslana strayed the path of his duty and instead found himself wandering the barren streets of Okhema long past Curtain-Fall Hour. He owed it to his multitude of experience from previous cycles to bypass Aglaea's threads, despite the effort it took. Eventually, without much thought, he found himself at the window of Phainon and Mydei's shared quarters.

Eleni slept peacefully in her crib. As a master of stealth, Khaslana faced little trouble entering the room unnoticed.

Slowly, he approached the crib, silently leaning over it to peer at the sleeping baby. She was even smaller than when Khaslana saw her last, that it was difficult to wrap his head around the fact that newborns could be so impossibly tiny.

She was incredibly adorable. Her little fists were clenched, and her cute nose was all scrunched up. It reminded Khaslana of Mydei when he was frustrated. She was dressed in a soft onesie that was undoubtedly Aglaea's handiwork, judging by the craft.

A baby mobile hung above Eleni's crib, adorned with little plush toys of baby chimeras and dromases that twirled softly in the lull of the room. While watching her, warmth that Khaslana hadn't felt in a long time began blooming in his chest.

“Hello,” Khaslana whispered fondly.

Suddenly, a pair of muffled voices rose outside. Khaslana tensed, preparing to leave at once, but the conversation that followed made him halt in his tracks.

“Mydei, you just completed Nikador's trial,” that was Phainon, sounding strained and desperate, “And you only just gave birth not too long ago.”

“My duty has not stopped,” Mydei responded firmly, “You know as well as I do that this is what needs to be done, especially now that I've become a demigod.”

"Still, you should rest a little longer. I—”

“Deliverer,” Mydei’s interruption cut cleanly through his protest, and Phainon fell silent. “There is no time. Era Nova is nigh. Lady Aglaea and Lady Tribios have already made that clear during today's meeting."

The silence stretched on.

“I know,” Phainon said finally, his voice subdued, “Forgive me. I was being irrational.”

There was a sigh on Mydei's end.

“I shall take my leave at the next Entry Hour,” Mydei announced, “The black tide grows stronger. I must defend Kremnos lest the city falls.”

“I know,” Phainon murmured, so softly Khaslana almost didn't hear him.

“After I leave, see to your duties. Claim Kephale's coreflame and lead us into Era Nova,” Mydei instructed, before he trailed off and his tone softened, “And take care of Eleni, okay? She deserves better.”

“She does,” Phainon agreed, “Don't worry, Mydei. I'll give it my all.”

"You will, you must," Mydei's voice nearly trembled from the firmness of his words, "Protect her with all that you have, Phainon."

"I promise," Phainon said in a heartbeat.

There was the rustle of movement, nothing Khaslana could properly make out but was sure he was rudely interrupting if he were to continue eavesdropping.

He turned and gave Eleni one last glance.

She deserves better, Mydei's words echoed in his head. Khaslana felt compelled to agree. She was such a sweet, cute little thing.

He needed to leave before her parents came in. Specifically Mydei, who was going to part ways with her soon. They likely wouldn't take him standing in their daughter's bedroom during Curtain-Fall Hour very well, and Khaslana wasn't prepared for a direct confrontation this early yet. 

When he left, it was with a heavy heart.

Phainon had said he would give it his all. Khaslana, too, had his work cut out for him.

Thousands of cycles slipped by, and still no dawn broke the endless night. The blood on Khaslana's hands had darkened beyond redemption.

He drove the crescent moon blade through Cyrene's chest with grim familiarity, yet the sight of her golden blood spilling in rivulets still seared through him. He never lingered long enough to watch the light fade from her shimmering blue eyes.

So the hunt for the coreflames began once anew.

Those people you swore to save, Professor Anaxa's words echoed in his head, They are no more than ants to you now, aren't they?

Khaslana's head pounded. His migraine felt like it was threatening to split his skull apart.

Sometimes, he wished he could just… stop. To take a breather, even briefly, from the weight of it all.

His weary steps carried him to the Grove, stirred by a longing to revisit the halls he had once walked as a bright-eyed student, side by side with his peers, with companions he had long since lost. He recalled the debates alongside the Nousporists, sitting in Anaxa's class, studying for final exams with Hyacine and Castorice. Had it really been so long?

Had so much time passed? Were the endless cycles leading him nowhere?

A familiar figure amid the quiet of the Grove gave him pause.

It had been ages since Khaslana last laid eyes on her, whereas she had been a tiny infant then, lulled to sleep by the baby mobile in her crib. Perhaps she had been born and lived numerous times since, yet their paths had simply not crossed.

This time, she was older. Eight years old, give or take.

Mydei was this age when he was fending for himself against sea monsters and the relentless waves in the Sea of Souls. Phainon was only a little older when his village was razed down and everyone he knew and loved brutally killed.

The child before him wore a beautiful yellow dress that seemed to hold a trace of sunlight, her blonde hair woven with white flowers. Khaslana stared for too long, because soon she had turned around and their eyes met, blue against golden.

He froze up like a deer caught in headlights.

Eleni's impassive face suddenly brightened with a smile. It made Khaslana's heart twinge, because she looked just like Mydei. He hadn't seen Mydei smile in a long, long time.

Without warning, Eleni dropped the book she was holding and dashed towards him, throwing her arms around his legs. It took everything in Khaslana not to recoil on instinct.

The coreflames, his mind screamed in alarm. Panic sparking through his chest, he quickly but gently pushed her away before she could get burned.

Luckily, Eleni didn't seem to notice through her excitement.

“Papa, you said you wouldn't be back until next week!” Eleni exclaimed, blinking wide joyful eyes up at him, “Did you come to surprise me?”

Khaslana hesitated. “... Yes,” he answered, tasting the lie on his tongue, “Aglaea gave me a short break, but I'll be going back very soon, so I still won't be home until then.”

“Oh,” Eleni sulked, mood dampened.

Khaslana looked around, uncertain of what to say. He was not the Phainon of this cycle, after all, and was only a tainted mimic of the man Eleni knew and loved as her father. The bond she sought wasn't his to claim.

“What are you doing at the Grove, Eleni?”

“Visiting!" Eleni replied cheerfully, “Mama’s busy, so I'm here. I was with Prof Nax, but he's teaching a class now. There's lots of cool books to read here.”

“That's good,” Khaslana said. He wanted to reach out to smooth the messy strands of locks escaping her braid, but decided against it. He would not risk harming a single hair on her head. “I hope you enjoy yourself to the fullest, Eleni.”

However, Eleni’s lips curved into a pout. Khaslana immediately panicked.

“Eleni?”

“Are you mad at me?” Eleni asked timidly, pouting harder. “You only call me ‘Eleni’ if it's something serious.”

Khaslana blinked. “I'm not mad,” he said automatically. A brief silence followed as he studied her face, then uncertainly, he tried, “Princess.”

“You're not?” Eleni challenged.

“I'm not,” Khaslana felt a chuckle rise from the back of his throat, which was almost startling. To him, that sensation felt foreign at this point. “I promise I'm not upset with you about anything, princess. I could never be.”

Eleni beamed again, obviously pleased, judging by the radiant smile that spread across her face. Her cheeks were so rosy and plump, her hair gleaming like the sun. Khaslana's chest tightened. He saw Mydei so vividly in her that it hurt.

Titans, he missed Mydei.

“I have to go now,” Khaslana murmured. He needed to leave before someone else, like Anaxa, walked in and saw him.

“Papa,” Eleni said.

“Yes, princess?”

“Are you okay?” She asked, and Khaslana's heart dropped, “Your eyes look sad.”

Sad? Khaslana thought his eyes looked hollow. Empty. He didn't want to loiter around Eleni for long lest she grow disturbed by the look in his eyes.

“I'm just a little tired,” Khaslana replied simply, a dire understatement. “Don't worry about me.”

Eleni frowned. “I'll tell Lady Agy to give you less work,” she declared with unwavering determination.

Khaslana couldn't help but laugh at her seriousness. “Thank you,” he mustered a genuine smile, though he wasn't sure for certain if it reached his eyes. Speaking of his eyes, he couldn't look directly at Eleni. He didn't want to frighten her. “I miss you and Mydei… very much.”

“I miss you too," Eleni exclaimed, “Mama misses you as well. But I’ll see you soon, Papa, so don’t be tired or sad!”

She was right. Khaslana felt his chest warm, not from the burning heat of the coreflames, but from overwhelming fondness. He returned her gaze with a small, tender smile. “I’ll see you soon, princess.”

When he left, Eleni waved at him. Khaslana waved back, then spun on his heel and never turned back.

The cycles reset. Again.

Khaslana killed Cyrene. A teenage, newly orphaned Phainon moved to Okhema, burning with the raw, untempered flames of vengeance and anger. The Flame-Chase Journey continued once more.

After nearly a million failures, Khaslana could move with a practiced precision born out of countless repetitions. It was a rhythm etched deeply and painfully into his bones, searing skin and tearing flesh. Negotiating for the coreflames was a ghost of a memory. Time had no mercy for the Deliverer.

Countless times he had struck and watched the golden blood drip. He felt it soak his palms, only to be replaced by the searing heat of the claimed coreflame, stolen from the heart of a corpse. A Chrysos Heir.

Holding onto so many coreflames had burned him from the inside out, rendering his physical vessel corroded. The memories of Khaslana were to be passed onto the Phainon of the current cycle, then the next, carried on endlessly until the dawn broke.

But so far, the horizon seemed to stretch on to no end, offering no glimpse of salvation within reach.

Nevertheless, Khaslana had to keep on trying.

Things were particularly grim this cycle.

Eleni was born. She was always born frail, her cries weaker than others and her heartbeat fragile as glass. Misfortune claimed her swiftly this cycle, and she had succumbed to illness at merely eight months old.

Those who were present at the quiet wards of the Twilight Courtyard that day, be it nurses or patients alike, would've heard the heart-wrenching, anguished scream that echoed through the corridor, only for the sound to fade into deathly silence.

After the child's burial, Mydei scarcely moved or spoke for two weeks, let alone ate or slept.

The Council of Elders, vicious as ever, are not as sympathetic to the loss. Rumours through the grapevine had spread like wildfire throughout Okhema, that Elder Caenis had heartlessly said, “As Chrysos Heirs, the Flame-Chase Journey and reclaiming of the coreflames must be your top priority. What is the small loss of an insignificant child born out of wedlock compared to the prophecy of the gods? As pawns, you must play your part.”

Phainon almost eviscerated her on the spot. It took three council members, Aglaea and the Ladies Tribios combined, to hold him back before he could tear her head from her shoulders.

Perhaps the grief was why, when confronted by the Flame Reaver, Mydei fought with more ferocity than usual.

He'd always been reckless and ruthless in battle, never caring much for his own life, but this was different. There was wildness burning through every strike, Khaslana realised that just as he narrowly dodged a punch to the ribs that would've sent him flying.

Through the slit of his mask, Khaslana could see it. Mydei's eyes, usually blazing with feral battle-thirst, were bloodshot. He looked like he hadn't slept in days. His grief seeped through every movement, every strike.

Despite bleeding and bruised black and blue, and having just lost his daughter, Mydei still stood with his back straight. He was a sheer force of will. He was magnificent.

His golden eyes flared with so much rage and resentment, charging towards Khaslana with a roar as he summoned a torrent of blood-red crystals.

But it was all futile. With a plunge of his blade into Mydei's tenth thoracic vertebrae, Mydei slumped over, gold oozing down tattoed skin.

As Mydei died, Khaslana held him. The crescent moon blade, stained with Mydei's blood, fell from his hands and hit the ground with a clatter. He pressed himself against Mydei's limp figure, feeling the warmth rapidly drain from him, uncaring of the golden ichor soaking into his own clothes.

With a shaky breath, he leaned forward and gently closed Mydei's eyelids, before throwing his mask aside and burying his face into Mydei's hair, whispering meaningless apologies to a man who could not hear them.

They stayed like that for ages.

Killing Mydei never got easier. Khaslana hoped it never did.

I need to hold onto this feeling, Khaslana constantly reminded himself, his grip tightening around Mydei's waist, the ever-burning coreflames scorching him from within, I must not let the Destruction consume me.

Remember this. Remember how it feels.

He closed his eyes, and imagined a happier ending. Golden wheat fields and swinging wind chimes. Mydei, alive and well, laughing and smiling with the easiness of a man unburdened by war and death. A baby's cry, a fragile little hand wrapped around his finger, grounding him in a world that didn't exist.

Khaslana opened his eyes. The world around him seemed drowned in death and despair. Eleni was gone. Mydei was gone. Phainon was alone, soon to bear the weight of the world. The Strife coreflame was in Khaslana's hands.

Remember this agony.

More cycles passed.

The dawn of Era Nova loomed over Amphoreus. Before facing the Flame Reaver, Mydei had entrusted an infant Eleni to Hyacine.

Khaslana had just killed Mydei. After Hyacine had passed Eleni to one of her assistants from the Twilight Courtyard, Khaslana killed her too.

He approached the Vortex of Genesis, where Phainon was waiting.

Phainon put up a good fight, but he had never outmatched Khaslana in any of the previous cycles, and neither would he in this one.

But with a swing of Dawnmaker and a slight misstep on Khaslana's part, the mask he wore to conceal his face fell, clattering to the ground.

Phainon let out a strangled gasp, “How—”

His shock was to be expected. Khaslana's face mirrored his own, except his features were cracked and marred from the corrosion to his physical form built up by millions of cycles.

“Phainon of Aedes Elysiae,” he said softly, “As you can see, you and I are one.”

“This— What is the meaning of this? How can this be?” Phainon’s eyes snapped towards him, wide and bulging, “Mydei, Eleni, they—”

“Mydei is dead,” Khaslana said simply, numb, “But Eleni is safe.”

If it were within Khaslana's control, no harm would ever come upon Eleni.

Phainon’s eyes burned with disbelief and barely contained fury. He sounded almost unhinged as he bellowed, “How can I trust you?”

“Because I was you,” Khaslana said. “And if you can understand that, then listen to me. Era Nova is a lie. If you lead Amphoreus into Era Nova, total annihilation will befall upon this world. Everyone has already died for a greater cause.”

Phainon was stunned for a brief moment, before barking out an empty laugh that would've chilled anyone's bones. He shook his head in disbelief, “Died for a greater cause?” he repeated, “What, you're trying to say the ends justify the means? Are everyone's lives just numbers to you?”

Numbers? Throughout the millions of cycles, Khaslana could recall with vivid clarity each and every death he had wrought, every life extinguished by his hands, up until the limits of his own mind and the scars of brain damage left only fragments behind.

But this feeling would remain with him forever.

“It will be up to you to make their deaths worth it,” Khaslana snapped. He remembered his promise with Cyrene. The sacrifices of the Flame-Chase Journey, the death of every beloved. “Be the Deliverer, and bring the dawn.”

He lifted the crescent moon blade, angling it right in front of his own chest.

Khaslana closed his eyes, and dreamed of a better tomorrow.

He prayed it would be worth it.

Cycle 33550336. The arrival of the strange outlanders calling themselves the Trailblazers.

It didn't take long for Phainon to like them, though wary as he was at first of outsiders who might pose a threat to Amphoreus. Caelus was friendly and cracked jokes Phainon didn't fully understand sometimes, while Dan Heng was more reserved but pleasant to be around, patient when sharing his knowledge on other worlds besides Amphoreus.

All in all, they were completely safe, very nice people.

“Ooh, is that her?”

“Caelus, be more polite,” Dan Heng admonished, but Phainon only laughed.

“Let me introduce you,” Phainon said, “This is Eleni. Princess, come say hello.”

The five year old girl, still clutching her father's hand, blinked up at the pair sleepily before smiling, “Hello!”

“Hello,” Dan Heng greeted, while Caelus gasped.

“Oh my god, she's a mini-Mydei.”

Phainon grinned. “She is,” he replied proudly, “She’s Mydei’s carbon copy.”

“Speaking of Mydei, I can't believe he trusted me enough to babysit,” Caelus said. “I don't think he likes me very much.”

“That's because I'll be here,” Dan Heng said. Caelus nodded solemnly.

“You're right,” he agreed without hesitation.

“Give yourself more credit, partner. You're more responsible than you realise when you put in the effort,” Phainon exclaimed, before turning to his daughter.

“That's not the assurance you think it is, but thanks,” he heard Caelus say distantly. He lowered onto one knee so he was eye-level to Eleni and pressed a kiss to her hand.

“Your adorable Highness, your faithful knight must now attend to some boring work for Lady Aglaea now, so be good while you spend some time with the Trailblazers, alright?” Phainon said fondly, “We shall reunite at Parting Hour for dinner. Mama will cook your favourites.”

“Okay!” Eleni beamed, seeming excited at the prospect of dinner, “Promise, mister knight?”

She extended a pinky finger, which Phainon linked with his own. “I promise,” he leaned forward and peppered kisses all over her cheeks, making her giggle. “See you later, princess.”

“We'll take good care of her,” Dan Heng added.

Caelus nodded along, “Don't worry, pal. I've got ample experience in babysitting. No sweat.”

“Ruan Mei’s creations do not count, Caelus,” Dan Heng sighed. “Don't mind him, Phainon. I'll keep an eye on both of them.”

“Thank you so much,” Phainon smiled gratefully, “Text me if anything happens,” his teleslate buzzed, then again and again, and he grimaced. “I might be running a little late. Then, I entrust my girl to you, Trailblazers.”

“Sure. See ya, Phainon.”

“Bye-bye, Papa,” Eleni said, pouting slightly as she reluctantly waved goodbye. Phainon ruffled her hair one last time before walking away.

Since it was nearing lunchtime, Caelus and Dan Heng decided to take Eleni out to eat. The restaurant’s owner seemed familiar with Eleni, patting her head affectionately and offering to serve a free plate of her favourite dessert, golden honeycakes drizzled with syrup.

“Is it alright to let her eat something so sugary?” Dan Heng muttered to Caelus quietly.

“Psh, it's fine. We're the fun uncles, remember?” Caelus answered. They both watched Eleni dig in, happily swinging her feet back and forth underneath the table. “Eleni, what do you like to do in your free time?”

Eleni chewed on a piece of honeycake before swallowing. “I like to read, eat, and play games!” she exclaimed, “And I like to be with Papa and Mama.”

Caelus grinned. “You sure love your Papa and Mama, huh?”

Nodding eagerly, Eleni put down her fork and spread her arms as wide as she could. “I love them this much!”

Dan Heng’s normally serious eyes softened. “I'm sure they love you very much too, Eleni.”

Eleni smiled, her cheeks full of sweet dessert.

“That’s an understatement. They’d go to the moon and back for you,” Caelus claimed. It was clear that Mydei and Phainon were incredibly protective and doted on her plenty. She was exceedingly precious to them.

The longer they remained on Amphoreus, the clearer that seemed.

The Flame Reaver was hot on their heels, relentless and unyielding in his pursuit of obtaining the coreflames. Everyone else was either dead or gone. Mydei had yelled for them to run to buy them time, and that was the last Caelus had seen of him. He feared that Mydei had fallen, too.

“I must go,” Phainon had told him, voice heavy with muted grief and cold resolve, “It is time to return Kephale's coreflame. Partner, I do not wish to involve you in our world’s problems any longer. You've done enough for us. But… I have one last request—”

“If it's within my power, of course I'll do it,” Caelus said. Phainon managed a faint smile.

“Look after my daughter for me and Mydei,” he said, “Please.”

Which was how Caelus ended up in the Vortex of Genesis, Mem fluttering around frantically behind him and a crying child clutched tightly against his chest.

Right. So the Flame Reaver, who had slaughtered the other Chrysos Heirs, was actually Phainon beneath the mask. As if dropping that lore bomb wasn’t staggering enough, Phainon started transforming. His body warped, turning into a roiling mass of black and crimson pixels. From the chaos sprouted vast and jagged wings, his cerulean eyes opening to reveal a radiant, divine gold.

Then the structure around them started crumbling. They began running, Caelus with his arms locked protectively around Eleni and his hand cupped around the back of her head, though golden shields had appeared above them, protecting them from any falling debris.

Phainon—Khaslana—was gone.

But within a blink, Mem, who had regained her memories as Cyrene, had safely whisked them away to an Aedes Elysiae of old.

“Where’s Eleni?” Caelus asked, chest tightening with panic as he looked around. She was gone. She had vanished from his arms. He couldn’t have lost her already, couldn’t have broken his promise to Phainon so soon.

Cyrene’s sparkly eyes softened. “I’m not sure for certain,’’ she said quietly, “But I believe she is not in any danger. Her existence is unique to this cycle, and to the others she was born in.”

“I gave Phainon my word that I’d look after her,” Caelus murmured, his heart twisting in his chest. “For him and for Mydei. They loved her so much. Even at the edge of death, all they cared about was her well-being.”

They didn’t deserve this. None of them did. It seemed only yesterday that Phainon had entrusted Eleni’s safety to Caelus and Dan Heng, and they were enjoying golden honeycakes together under a gentler sky.

“Don’t worry,” Cyrene’s soft voice carried warmth, a hopeful hum in her tone, “I have a feeling that their family will find one another again, when a gentler dawn and a better tomorrow arrives.”

Thirty million cycles, thirty million failures, and at last, the sun rose, its light cleaving through the eternal night. The blazing sun that was destined to rise.

The sacrifices of the Flame-Chase Journey had not been for naught. 

The battle against Irontomb had been arduous. Rebuilding what had been lost would take time, but for the first time in millions of thousands of years, the people of Amphoreus could finally look towards the future. With the help of the Trailblazers and their allies, Amphoreus was on its steady path of recovery. 

In addition, the Chrysos Heirs could finally take a break. 

Phainon, who had inherited all the memories and experiences of Khaslana after the end of the cycles, felt oddly out of place in this new era of peace. To be fair, he had gone from being trapped in a neverending loop of slaughtering his companions, merging with a scepter, which was horrible—zero out of ten experience, by the way—then going on to take down a Lord Ravager.

It felt like waking up from a long nightmare. A very, very long nightmare. He still woke up in the dead of night haunted by the phantom burn of coreflames in his chest, but when he reached down, there was nothing there anymore. 

Even worse, despite the Flame-Chase Journey finally ending, duty was still keeping him and Mydei apart. Their last real encounter was when Mydei had pulled him in by the collar and kissed him passionately in the wake of Irontomb's fall, right in front of the other Chrysos Heirs, the Trailblazers, the Genius Society, and other factions who had come to join the fight. 

They were supposed to retire from being the world's heroes, but Mydei was still preoccupied with issues regarding his countrymen and his obligations as their ruler. If Phainon were less mature about it, he'd sulk. 

Today's council meeting with Aglaea took longer than usual, discussing the temporary relocation of baby chimeras as the Garden of Life was under reconstruction. Tired, Phainon dragged himself home, expecting to return to an empty house, and was pleasantly surprised to find Mydei already there.

Phainon blinked, and his prior exhaustion had dissipated like smoke. "Mydei! You’re back early.”

“I've already sorted out the most important of my tasks,” Mydei replied. He crooked a finger in invitation and beckoned Phainon over.

Phainon’s feet moved without thinking, making a beeline towards the gorgeous beauty reclining on the bed. Mydei extended his arms, and that was all the permission Phainon needed. The mattress dipped under his weight as Phainon settled against him, resting his head on Mydei’s chest and wrapping his arms around his waist.

He let out a small breath, finding a shameful amount of comfort in the steady rhythm of Mydei’s heartbeat. Often, he fell asleep best to the sound of it pressed against his ear. 

A hand carded through his hair. “Deliverer,” that familiar voice called, and Phainon hummed in recognition. “We haven't gotten the chance to talk properly. How have things been?”

“Fine. Smoother than I anticipated, actually,” Phainon answered, though it wasn't as if he ever doubted Aglaea's abilities, and with her humanity restored, it was surprisingly easy to get close to her. “Things have been peaceful. It's not a bad change, but I'm still getting used to it."

“It has,” Mydei agreed, before pausing. “I wanted to tell you something.”

Phainon reached out, laying his hand gently over Mydei’s. With Aquila’s false sky gone, Amphoreus was no longer trapped in eternal daylight. The curtains swayed, and pale moonlight streamed through in slender beams.

“What is it?” he asked softly.

The sheets rustled as Mydei adjusted himself to sit upright. “I've been dreaming about her,” Mydei murmured. “About Eleni.”

For a brief moment, Phainon's breath stilled. He exhaled slowly, thumb brushing over Mydei's knuckles. “Do you miss her?”

“Ever since I learned of her existence.”

Phainon understood the feeling. Across all the cycles where Eleni existed, they had never gotten the chance to watch her grow up and reach adulthood. 

He missed her dearly already. He missed the sound of her laughter, the warmth of her tiny hands, the way her presence had made the crushing weight of the world seem the slightest bit easier to bear. With no divine prophecies and world-destroying cataclysms to worry about, the ache of her absence only cut deeper.

“I miss her too,” Phainon murmured, his words heavy with longing. He wanted to see her take her first steps again, stumble through her first words, and live long enough to flourish and find her own place in this new world.

He lifted his head, and his eyes met Mydei's. Mydei had a small, wistful smile on his face, along with the same gleam in his golden eyes that Phainon had fallen irrevocably in love with across lifetimes. Sometimes he still found it unfathomable that Mydei reciprocated that love despite all the unforgivable things Phainon had done to him.

Even after knowing Phainon was a vessel created for hatred and destruction, Mydei still looked at him and believed him capable of love.

“Like what you see?” Phainon teased, after a moment of prolonged eye-contact.

Huffing, Mydei tried to pull his hand away from where it caressed the sun tattoo on Phainon's neck, but Phainon caught his hand in time and kissed his palm. He exhaled slowly. The warmth there was a familiar comfort.

“You’re too good to me, Mydei,” he whispered.

Mydei reached out, fingers brushing against Phainon’s cheek, his touch so gentle it almost hurt.

“You’ve spent too long punishing yourself for what couldn’t be undone. I don’t plan to add to that weight,” Mydei said. “None of those thirty million cycles were futile failures. Your sacrifices have borne fruit, and your duties have been fulfilled. It’s not selfish for you to have dreams of your own again. So, Deliverer, will you share those dreams with me?”

At the declaration, a breath trembled in Phainon’s chest. For the first time in ages, the endless ache in his chest quieted, no longer burning at the hollow of loss. He let out a sound between a sigh and a laugh.

“Dreams, huh,” he echoed. For so long, his dreams had been to fulfill everyone else’s dreams. To dream for himself felt foreign, almost forbidden. Khaslana did not have the privilege to dream, after the seeds of chaos sown by his own hands.

When he searched within his heart, however, the truth was simple. All he wanted was for the Chrysos Heirs to live in happiness, for Mydei to remain by his side, and for them to build a life free of strife and war. He wanted them to welcome their daughter once more, to raise their family together in a better Amphoreus, and let that love take root and flourish until the end of time.

Mydei’s expression was fond, softened by a vulnerability the him of the cycles had never been granted. His eyes glimmered like dawn breaking over still waters. The face of a god who had lowered his weighty crown.

“I don’t think you even have to tell me anything,” Mydei chuckled, his chest rumbling lowly in a manner that made Phainon’s heart race. He lightly flicked Phainon on the nose. “It’s written all over your face.”

“Mydeimos,” Phainon whined, turning over and propping himself up on his elbows. A faint pout curved his lips, the sight of it making Mydei snort.

In the next second, Mydei shifted, the loose fabric of his sleeves sliding down his shoulders, revealing bare skin inked with crimson tattoos that wound intricately across the planes of his muscles.

Phainon swallowed, an emotion long neglected stirring within him. Desire. “Mydei—”

“Do I have to spell this out for you too, Deliverer?” Mydei asked, parting his legs wider beneath Phainon. “Don’t keep me waiting.”

Suddenly, the aftermath of divine duty and endless penance were forgotten in an instant. Phainon leaned forward, and Mydei met him halfway, two halves of a whole.

Nine months later, a tiny bundle was placed carefully into Mydei’s waiting arms.

Mydei’s hair clung to his temples, his skin damp with sweat, but the moment he looked down at the newborn, his exhaustion seemed to melt away. Her small fists were curled tight, her cheeks flushed the colour of dawn. She let out a soft, uncertain cry before settling against his arms.

The longer he stared, tears began to gather in his eyes. “It’s been so long,” he murmured, voice on the verge of trembling as he pulled her close to his chest. “My lovely child, it’s so good to see you again. I promise to do you right this time. I swear it.”

Phainon sat next to the bed, almost in a daze, as if the world around them had fallen into a hush. He didn't even register Hyacine and Little Ica leaving the room. Seeing Mydei cradle Eleni for the first time was a sight forever etched in his mind, but witnessing Mydei's tears was the last straw.

His vision blurred. “She’s beautiful, Mydei,” he stammered through the emotions choked up in his throat. “I— I—”

He heard Mydei laugh at him wetly. “Pull yourself together, Deliverer." he teased, “You've done this before. Come say hello to your daughter.”

Phainon wasted no time. Eleni was still so small and precious, and there were tiny tufts of downy golden hair on the top of her head. Just like the first time all those cycles ago, he couldn't quite believe that she was real. That she was here. That she was theirs.

He was so, so afraid he'd break her, but right now, all he wanted was to be close to her. 

“Hello again, princess,” Phainon whispered. A faint smile tugged at his lips, though his eyes shimmered. “I’ve missed you. I’m so honoured to be your father again, in this life, and every one that follows.”

He leaned forward until his chin rested against Mydei’s shoulder, the familiar scent of him grounding Phainon in the moment. Mydei let out a soft breath and melted into the contact, their bodies fitting together with the ease of souls that had found each other too many times to count.

Together, they gazed down at their tiny miracle in Mydei’s arms. The world around them was quiet and whole for the first time in what felt like eternity.

Eleni was with them again, and that was all that mattered.

In every cycle Eleni existed, their main concern had always been the weak constitution she was born with.

“I won't afford repeating any mistakes,” Mydei had said firmly, undoubtedly reminded of and traumatised by the particular cycle Eleni had passed from sickness, “I won't— I refuse to lose her like that again.”

Phainon shared the sentiment. This time, they would give her the life she wholly deserved and more.

Shortly after being born, Eleni had difficulty sleeping. Phainon would spend hours soothing her cries and ensuring she went to bed comfortably, which he saw no problem with considering he hardly slept anyway and Mydei deserved time to recuperate from childbirth, in spite of Mydei's protests to share the workload.

Unfortunately, Eleni also had problems feeding. This always devastated Mydei. He constantly sought pediatricians at the Twilight Courtyard for help, running himself ragged with worry that he wasn't feeding Eleni enough and he was starving her, though thankfully Eleni gradually improved at latching as time passed.

Phainon was equally as relieved. On one hand he was glad Eleni was getting the nutrition she needed. On the other hand, it was a huge weight off Mydei's shoulders.

Still, they were still so worried. Their princess was just so small, after all.

Every morning, the first thing Phainon and Mydei would do was check on her. They'd spend a good half of Lucid Hour simply laying in bed with Eleni between them, cuddling her and showering her with kisses. Mydei liked to stroke his fingers through her thin hair while Phainon would blow raspberries into her stomach to make her giggle. Then, Mydei would feed her.

On days they had errands to tend to, they were reluctant to part with her in the mornings. If they could, they would spend all their time with her, attached to her as they were. Thankfully, thanks to the fact there were no more prophecies or monsters, most of their time could be spent together.

And on days they brought her out of the house, either one of them would insist on carrying her everywhere. Even after she learned how to crawl and walk, her feet never touched the ground unless she put up a fuss.

“Hello!” Cyrene arrived at their house one day to greet them, having just returned to Amphoreus to visit not long ago after embarking on an expedition with the Astral Express. She squealed, “Eleni, my dear, you've grown so much since the last time I saw you! Come give Aunty Reney a hug.”

She bent down and slipped her arms beneath Eleni to lift the child up. A small grunt escaped her as Eleni settled solidly against her chest. “Oh my,” Cyrene said with a surprised laugh, shifting her grip, “You're heavier than I thought.”

That was the same thing Tribbie had said when she saw Eleni earlier, exclaiming that it wouldn't be long before Eleni was going to surpass her in height. Aglaea had informed Phainon that she would be sending him a batch of new hand-sewn clothes for Eleni soon, in case she outgrew her current ones before the next season.

Hyacine had a similar reaction when they brought Eleni to see her for a check-up just last week. “She weighed only five pounds when she was born, so I'm pleasantly surprised to see how big she is now!” Hyacine had said.

“Really?” Phainon had asked, unconvinced, Eleni sitting snugly in his lap, babbling and drooling all over his sleeve. He and Mydei both still thought Eleni was too tiny for her age.

Mydei leaned over and wiped away a string of drool from her lip, “Are you hungry, sweetheart? Mama will feed you after this.”

Eleni had just turned two, though Mydei still insisted on breastfeeding her. He would wean her off eventually, but not this soon. Perhaps it was Mydei's breastmilk and the frequent feedings that resulted in Eleni suddenly shooting up a percentile.

On the streets, citizens would stop to say hello. Multiple times, people fondly remarked that Eleni took after her parents in height and they would wish for her continued health and happiness.

When Anaxa saw her on his rare trip to Okhema from the Grove, he'd raised one eyebrow. “Has it really been so long since I saw her last? When did she turn five years old?”

“She’s actually two, Professor,” Phainon corrected, pressing a smushy kiss to Eleni's soft cheek. He rubbed her chubby arms before adjusting her chimera hairpin that was coming loose. “Princess, are you hungry? We'll go meet up with Mama soon.”

Anaxa let out a baffled noise. “Two? Don't be ridiculous. I’d wager she'd weigh about the same as a baby dromas,” he shook his head in disbelief, “That’s the chunkiest baby I've ever seen. I don't think I'd even be able to carry her.”

“I can carry her fine, though.”

Anaxa gave him a deadpan look. “That’s because you're you, Phainon. And the average two year old is not this tall. It's either you and Mydeimos’ giant genes are finally kicking in, or you two have been overfeeding her.”

Overfeeding? Phainon didn't quite see it. Other people didn't know how much it had broken his and Mydei's hearts to hear her cries from being unable to feed. To them, as long as their princess was well-fed and healthy, then nothing else mattered.

A tiny hand patted his arm. “Papa,” Eleni said, blinking wide golden eyes at him expectantly. “Mama?”

Phainon chuckled. “Yes, yes, we’ll go see Mama.” He scooped her up with effortless ease, his grin widening at the sound of her bright giggles. “Your faithful knight shall escort you, my dearest princess.”

He couldn’t wait to see what kind of person his and Mydei’s little princess would grow into. Maybe she’d wield a sword like a warrior of Kremnos, study among the scholars of the Grove, or learn to heal at the Twilight Courtyard. Whatever she chose, Phainon couldn’t wait to see her chase her dreams. And someday, she might even fall in love and get married—

No. Absolutely not. On second thought, marriage was definitely out of the question. That part could wait forever.

Phainon was perfectly content for her to remain his little princess, always.

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

An instrument of destruction could not be capable of a touch so gentle.

Khaslana only destroyed everything he touched. Naturally, even after the hundreds of thousands of coreflames within him had disappeared for good, only time could heal such fresh wounds.

Eleni, daughter of Mydeimos, was the most precious existence in the entire universe. Khaslana had mourned for her in every cycle she had existed and in every cycle he had failed her. He loved her so, so much that he'd tear apart an Aeon if it meant she would be happy and healthy.

His past failures as a hero, as a partner, as a father, haunted him.

Phainon awoke with a jolt, bolting upright with his pulse thundering in his ears. His hair was plastered to his forehead with cold sweat, blinking rapidly as his blurry vision gradually cleared. The dimness of their bedroom was still a foreign thing, he had grown too familiar with waking up in the dead of the night to the sunlight of Kephale's Dawn Device streaming in through the windows.

The room slowly stopped swimming. Phainon willed his breathing to steady, but the tremor in his hands wouldn't stop. He pressed his palms into his sternum until his breathing stuttered back into something normal, the inside of his eyelids stinging uncomfortably.

“Deliverer?” A voice asked groggily. Phainon froze.

He opened his mouth, but no words came out. His mouth felt as dry as sandpaper. The sheets rustled as Mydei sat up and leaned against the headboard with one hand cradling his gravid stomach.

Guilt washed over him, something ugly pricking at his chest for waking Mydei up when he needed all the rest he could get. “Go back to sleep,” Phainon whispered, rubbing a hand over his eyes. “It’s nothing.”

“It doesn't seem like nothing,” Mydei answered.

Okay, Mydei was probably right. “I can handle it,” Phainon protested, however, “I’m fine, Mydei. It’s just a nightmare.”

A beat of silence passed. Phainon was almost convinced Mydei had taken his suggestion, but he should’ve known better. The sheets rustled again as Mydei shifted, “Deliverer, come here.”

Phainon turned to glance at him. Mydei had his arms spread in invitation, a teasing quirk tugging at his lips, “I'll soothe you back to sleep, you big baby.”

“I—” Phainon faltered. A sharp ache of fear made his heart hammer so hard he thought it'd lurch out of his chest. He stared at Mydei, his beautiful Mydei, from the flicker of concern on his face to the curve of his rounded belly beneath his robes. “I can't.”

How could the incarnation of hatred, the prisoner of flames, dare to seek salvation?

Mydei's eyes softened, warm enough to make the burning fire in Phainon's chest suddenly feel small.

“Come here,” Mydei repeated, insistent, “I’m not made of glass, Deliverer. I'm sturdier than you think.”

Mydei was sturdier and tougher than anybody Phainon knew, but even he had fallen time and time again to his blade.

Phainon hesitated, but the endless patience in Mydei's eyes drew him in. Sometimes, he still didn't understand how someone could look at him with so much open affection, but time and time again, Mydei had proven it was possible.

He edged forward, careful and still hesitant, pressing himself into the shelter of Mydei's arms and tucked his face into the familiar slope of Mydei's shoulder. His body was rigid, every sinew wound tight with fear as he braced for disaster, but then Mydei's arms wrapped around him and Phainon felt himself melt into the safety of his embrace, the hellfire in him quieting.

“I’m sorry I woke you,” Phainon murmured, his voice muffled into Mydei's shoulder. Mydei hummed and smoothed a palm up and down Phainon's back. He bent his head and dropped a gentle kiss on Phainon's hair, the kind only reserved for tender moments like this.

Then he felt it. A soft thump beneath his skin. Mydei's breath stilled. Phainon jerked, pulling back as his hand hovered above Mydei's abdomen in wonder.

“Did you feel that?” Phainon’s voice nearly cracked on the question, “She kicked!”

Mydei grinned. “Seems like she wanted to comfort you too,” he said lightly. He caught Phainon’s hand and guided it towards his stomach. “Go on. She’s waiting.”

Phainon let out a tiny, disbelieving whimper as his palm settled over the place their daughter had kicked. “Hi, princess,” he whispered in awe. “It’s me.”

Another nudge tapped against his hand, and Phainon let out a shaky laugh, “She’s pretty active, isn't she?”

“Of course she is.” Mydei shifted, easing himself upright so he could see Phainon’s face clearly. “She’s your daughter. Besides, she’s more than familiar with your voice. You talk to her every day.”

Phainon flushed, “I just… like telling her things.”

“What things?” Mydei asked, teasing.

“Just… stuff.”

Mydei arched a brow. “Stuff like how you’re terrified of messing everything up?”

Phainon made a sheepish face. “You heard that?”

“Deliverer, you whisper to my stomach. I’m pregnant, not deaf.”

Phainon groaned and buried his face in the crook of Mydei’s neck. Mydei laughed softly and combed his fingers through Phainon’s hair until the tension ebbed out of him again.

“She’ll be fine,” Mydei assured, “She loves you.”

But this was the first time Eleni would be born outside of the cycles. Phainon felt a sense of duty to do her right this time, to give her the life she always deserved. He was terribly afraid of fucking that up. Somehow, Mydei still had so much confidence in him.

He turned his head just enough to murmur quietly, “I want to be good for her. For you.”

“You already are, idiot,” Mydei replied without missing a beat.

Another soft kick punctuated the words. Mydei smirked down at him, “See? She agrees.”

Phainon leaned up to kiss him, gentle and breathless. “I love her,” he whispered, hopelessly enamoured. “I love you.”

Mydei kissed him back. His steady assurance was enough to make Phainon feel grounded again, the knot in his chest finally loosening as he let himself smile. “I know.”

As always, Eleni was so small. If Phainon hadn't been scared before, he definitely was now by at least tenfold. His biggest fear was doing anything that might hurt her at all.

Mydei had just finished feeding her. It had been a struggle from the start. Eleni had trouble latching, her tiny face all scrunched up as she rooted and whined, hunger making her increasingly restless. Although Mydei tried to soothe her, the harder she cried the more his own composure frayed.

By the time she finally latched on and suckled properly, Mydei was understandably relieved but exhausted.

His lover needed a break. Eleni had thankfully stopped crying, but judging by her yawns she was clearly getting sleepy. Phainon kissed Mydei's temple and whispered assuringly, “I'll put her to bed.”

He cradled her as carefully as possible, the weight of her against his chest always making something protective and fragile coil tight inside him. Any wrong move and he knew he would never forgive himself. His steps were slow and measured as he walked across the room.

An old, familiar rhythm returned without much thought, the gentle sway from heel to toe and the faintest rocking motion that had once soothed her on sleepless nights in lives before this one. Eleni stirred once, a tiny sound puffing against his collarbone, her small fist curling against his shirt before relaxing again.

Phainon swallowed. He was suddenly overwhelmed by how much he adored her.

Without thinking, he began humming a tune to the rhythm of his steps. It slipped out of him instinctively, threading itself into the quiet of the room as naturally as breathing. 

It was a song from a land of golden wheat fields and wind chimes dangling from wooden porches, a place where the days were long and the evenings smelt of warm earth. He remembered his mother singing it as she chopped vegetables in their tiny kitchen, and a young Cyrene swinging back and forth on her favourite swing, humming the same melody as she shuffled her cards.

The Phainons across all cycles had hummed this song to his daughter, whereas Khaslana hadn't thought about this song in years. 

Eleni settled against his arms, out like a light. Phainon exhaled, standing stock-still as he let his gaze trace every softened line of her face. Gingerly, he shifted his stance, extra careful not to wake her. 

“Have you discovered a second passion as a singer, Deliverer?”

Phainon held back the embarrassing choked noise that threatened to escape his throat. He cautiously lowered their daughter into her crib before swivelling around, turning towards Mydei, who he thought had long dozed off. “It’s just a lullaby that was popular in my hometown,” he muttered. 

“I know. I’ve heard it,” Mydei said, “It sounds beautiful.”

Phainon’s gaze never left Mydei as he approached the bed. Mydei’s sweaty hair clung to his forehead, the blonde strands plastered in uneven arcs, and the loose sleeves of his robes pushed down to bunch at his naked chest. Deep, shadowed crescents dragged beneath his eyes. Neither of them had gotten much sleep since Eleni’s birth. Sleep deprivation was a constant in the early days of parenthood, something they both knew well. 

“You should sleep through the night,” Phainon said. It would only be a matter of time before Eleni woke up crying again. “I can handle it.”

“She’ll be hungry. I need to feed her,” Mydei murmured, adjusting his crumpled robes. 

Phainon slipped into the space beside him, hand reaching up to smoothen the worried crease between Mydei’s brows. “It scares me how light she feels in my arms,” he admitted. He knew Mydei felt the same way. 

From the way Mydei stiffened, it was painfully clear what memory had seized him. Phainon felt something twist sharply in his chest. It had been torture for Phainon, but witnessing Mydei’s grief back then had made it borderline unbearable, the way he had sobbed and screamed, sounds Phainon had never believed could come from him, before the light finally bled from his eyes altogether. 

The echo of that loss haunted the space between them now. 

Mydei’s jaw worked, a flicker of old fear passing through his tired eyes. His gaze drifted towards the crib, “I can’t watch it happen again, Phainon,” he exhaled. 

Phainon held him close in silent reassurance. 

The tragedies of the past would not repeat. He would make sure of that. 

Eleni grew up beautifully. And Phainon cherished watching every step of her growth. 

He remembered the tiny fists that clung to his shirt, how her entire hand could wrap around his finger. Her first word had been Mama. Her first steps had been towards Phainon, uncertain wobbly toddling before she happily tumbled forward into Phainon’s arms. She stood taller now, brighter but still unmistakably the small newborn he could once hold in one arm and loved no less than before she was born. 

She also looked more and more like Mydei with every passing day, which was something Phainon delighted in. 

One morning, Phainon awoke to a small palm patting his cheek. He opened his eyes, blue meeting golden. Eleni’s golden hair was like a lion’s mane, which meant she had just woken up and Mydei had yet to sit her down and meticulously braid her hair. 

“Good morning, Papa!”

Phainon smiled, “Good morning, princess.” He glanced to the side and noticed Mydei’s side of the bed was empty. “Is Mama making breakfast?”

Eleni nodded, her wide eyes staring at him expectantly. 

“Is there something on my face?” he joked, feigning oblivion.

“Papa,” Eleni whined, her lip twisting into an exaggerated pout, one that hardly lasted a heartbeat before a startled shriek burst out of her. Phainon had swooped in, wrapping his arms around her and tackling her gently onto the bed. His fingers dug playfully into her sides as he tickled her, peppering her cheeks and forehead with quick, noisy kisses.

Eleni dissolved into a fit of uncontrollable giggles, her legs kicking uselessly as she tried to squirm away. “No— Papa! Stop—!” she wheezed through laughter. “Mama, help—”

Footsteps shuffled into the bedroom. “Deliverer,” Mydei said, exasperated. Phainon looked up, grinning. “Don’t overdo it.”

“Mama!” Eleni cried, “Papa forgot what day it is!”

Mydei clicked his tongue. “Did he? How unforgivable,” he approached the bed and sat down, “What punishment do you think might be fitting, Eleni?”

“No cake for Papa!” Eleni declared, crossing her arms with all the seriousness of a monarch issuing a decree. Well, she was a princess. 

“That’s harsh!” Phainon groaned dramatically, pressing a hand to his heart. “Your own daughter, turning against you… Princess, won’t you forgive your father?”

Mydei smirked. “It’s a very reasonable sentence, I’d say.”

Phainon lunged playfully to scoop her up again, but she squealed and dove into Mydei’s lap for protection, sweet peals of laughter ringing through the room. 

“Aw, Papa’s just messing with you, sweetie.” Phainon laughed, ruffling her hair. “Happy fifth birthday.”

Eleni’s eyes widened, her pout immediately melting into a bright, toothy grin. “You remembered!” she squeaked, bouncing in place.

“Of course I did,” Phainon leaned down and tapped her nose. “How could I forget the most important day of the year?”

Mydei let out a soft snort. “Nice save.”

Eleni giggled, leaping up and throwing her arms around Phainon’s neck, squeezing tight. 

Phainon lifted her with ease, pressing a kiss to the top of her head. “Even our friends from the Astral Express have come to say happy birthday,” he gave her a teasing look, “But only if the birthday girl can make it there without exploding from excitement first.”

“I won’t explode!” she protested, then immediately burst into laughter too big for her small body.

Mydei shook his head affectionately, brushing a stray strand of hair from her face, his eyes soft and fond. “Mama wishes you a very happy birthday as well, Eleni. You are a blessing, both your father’s and mine.”

Eleni’s grin stretched from ear to ear, her cheeks flushed with pure glee, and she let go of Phainon to throw her arms around him in a tight hug. 

As Mydei hugged her back, Phainon watched the scene with a soft, contended smile.

“Happy birthday, dearest Eleni,” Aglaea said, her eyes warm. “I have prepared your presents. Have your father carry them back after the celebrations.”

“Thank you, Lady Agy!” Eleni beamed. 

The other Chrysos Heirs were also in attendance. Anaxa asked, sounding somewhat unconvinced, “And you’re five this year, correct?”

“Mhm!”

Anaxa didn’t seem to quite believe this. “Right.”

“She had a growth spurt,” Mydei explained, cutting a slice of cake. He sounded proud. 

When the Trailblazers showed up, Caelus rushed forward and lifted her up. “Happy birthday!” he screeched, “Oh my god, I’m getting emotional. You were the size of a bean like, yesterday.”

“Caelus, put her down,” Dan Heng chided. 

“It’s fine,” Mydei sighed, as Eleni giggled while Caelus spun her around.

Phainon lifted her effortlessly next, twirling her once before setting her down. “You’re too fast for me, little whirlwind!”

Eleni squealed in pure delight. As she ran off to greet Hyacine and Castorice, her little dress fluttering behind her, Mydei and Phainon exchanged a look, both silently marvelling at how much she had grown, yet how bright and full of life she remained.

“Our girl’s all grown up,” Phainon murmured. Now he was getting emotional too. 

“She’s five, Deliverer,” Mydei laughed, “Still got a long way to go before she grows up. Unless…”

Phainon cocked his head, smiling in confusion, “Unless?”

“Want to have another?”

Phainon almost dropped his plate of cake. Mydei laughed harder, before casually walking away to check on their daughter, leaving Phainon a sputtering mess after him.
